newsitem.title: FRANCE: Morocco seen slowing down wheat import pace.
newsitem.headline: Morocco seen slowing down wheat import pace.

text.p: Moroccan wheat imports are expected to continue at a slower pace in coming months in the face of a bumper crop and following a summer grain buying spree, European grain traders said on Tuesday.
Since July 1 Moroccan public and private importers have bought a total of 500,000 tonnes of grain, including 300,000 tonnes of soft wheat, on world markets.
"Imports will now proceed at a slower pace," one trader predicted.
Traders linked the summer import frenzy to Morocco's recent economic liberalisation that unleashed speculative buying.
But now things are cooling down a bit, allowing millers faced with a bumper crop at home to process the imported grain.
"Future purchases will hinge on the levels of grain stocks in the mills," one trader said.
Another trader also said that a record crop put Morocco in a position to delay future purchases in anticipation world prices will ease further.
Moroccan authorities expect a record grain crop of 9.6 million tonnes in 1996 after severe drought slashed the 1995 grain harvest to 1.7 million tonnes.
In its latest monthly report the International Grains Council predicted Moroccan production of wheat, including durum, at 5.5 million tonnes and imports at 900,000 tonnes in 1996.
Morocco imported a total of 3.7 million tonnes of cereals including 3.0 million tonnes of wheat in 1995/96 (July/June), Moroccan grain officials have said.
